[[Category:Recipes using Dijon mustard]]

This '''savory mustard sauce''' is great on filet mignon or pork tenderloin, or as a grilling baste for chicken.

== Ingredients ==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Dijon Mustard|Dijon mustard]]
* ¼ cup chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* 1 ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¼ tsp freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallot]], very finely [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 3 tbsp unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided

== Procedure ==
#Heat olive oil in a large slope-sided [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium high heat. Add shallot and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until golden.
#Meanwhile, combine broth and starch. Set aside.
#Once shallot has cooked, add mustard, salt, and pepper to pan. Decrease heat to medium low heat.
#Once sauce heats to just below a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], add broth mixture. Cook, whisking continuously, until sauce thickens slightly.
#Whisk in butter 1 tbsp at a time, waiting for the one before it to fully melt before adding another.
#Once all butter has been used, remove sauce from heat.
#Serve with a steak or some pork tenderloin, or use as a grilling baste.
